why: Removal runs before addition, so an interrupted promotion leaves an issue with no priority label instead of two -- and an issue with no horizon is one the refill never sees again. The write-order test fails on the call order; the interrupted-promotion test fails because the rate-limited DELETE now runs first and the issue never gains priority:now.
killedBy: queue plan application writes additions before removals so an interrupted write never leaves an issue without a horizon
reconcile command leaves an interrupted promotion with two horizons, never none, and hands it to the audit
